To: Claims and underwriting staff, all regions
From: Personal Lines Underwriting
Date: November 15, 2024
Re: UW-25-01, HO-2025 edition: percentage wind and hail deductible

Form HO-2025 replaces HO-2023 for losses on or after January 1, 2025. The edition that applies is set by the date of loss, not the date the claim is reported, so a 2024 loss reported in 2025 is still handled under HO-2023.

In the West and South regions, the deductible for windstorm or hail becomes 2% of the Coverage A limit instead of a flat $1,000. On a home in Colorado at the state's median Coverage A of $414,000, the deductible for a wind or hail claim is now $8,280. On a home in Texas at the state's median Coverage A of $261,000, the deductible for a wind or hail claim is now $5,220. In the North and East regions, wind and hail keep the $1,000 deductible.

Two other terms change in every region. The fungi, mold and wet rot sublimit falls from $10,000 to $5,000, and a roof surface more than 15 years old on the date of loss is settled at actual cash value rather than replacement cost.

Expect fewer and larger wind and hail payments in the West and South regions from the spring of 2025, and more of those claims closed without payment because the damage falls below the deductible. Explain the deductible in dollars on first contact, so the insured is not surprised by the decision.

hits.header: CL-25-14 memo: Roofing labor and material costs, Denver metro, third quarter 2025
hits.body:
To: West region claims staff
From: Claims Cost Management
Date: October 15, 2025
Re: CL-25-14, Roofing labor and material costs, Denver metro, third quarter 2025

Roofing contractors in the Denver metro area raised their prices by about 22 percent for work billed from July 1 to September 30, 2025. The increase covers labor and materials alike. Crews are still committed to repairs from the April hail storm (CAT-25-07), and shingle and underlayment prices rose over the same months.

We reviewed the Colorado hail and wind claims closed in the quarter, 167 in all. Their repair costs run about 22 percent above what the same scope of work cost before July. The change is in the price of the work, not in the damage: the number of roofing squares and the items on the estimates are in line with earlier claims.

Do not question estimates that reflect the new prices. Reserve open Colorado roof claims at current prices, and use the price list dated July 1, 2025 in the estimating system. We will review again at the end of the fourth quarter.

hits.header: Homeowners Policy, Form HO-2025 | 7. Duties After Loss | edition HO-2025
hits.body:
In case of a loss to covered property, we have no duty to provide coverage under this policy if the failure to comply with the following duties is prejudicial to us. You must see that the following are done:

hits.title: Payments platform outage, May 11 to 22, 2026
hits.header: OPS-26-03 memo: Payments platform outage, May 11 to 22, 2026
hits.body:
To: All claims staff
From: Claims Operations
Date: June 8, 2026
Re: OPS-26-03, Payments platform outage, May 11 to 22, 2026

The payments platform failed to deliver claim payments issued from May 11 to 22, 2026. The 133 payments issued in that window, on 118 claims and totaling $953,540.43, were voided. Of these, 95 were indemnity payments and 38 were expense payments.

Each voided payment was reissued for the same amount to the same payee from May 26 to June 5, 2026. No claim was paid twice and none was paid less. Payees received their money two to three weeks late.

The voids and reissues distort paid-loss reports by payment date. A report that counts voided payments shows money in May that was never delivered, and one that ignores reissues misses it in late May and early June. Count reissued payments and exclude voided ones, which is how the reporting views are built.

If an insured or a vendor asks about a late payment from this period, confirm the reissue date on the claim and apologize for the delay. Section 6 of the claims handling guidelines covers how a voided payment is reissued.

hits.header: CG-2026 guideline: Property Claims Handling Guidelines | 3. Hail inspection procedure

3.6 Compare the estimate with the deductible before writing it up. Under HO-2025 in the West and South regions, many hail losses fall below 2% of Coverage A.

hits.header: CG-2026 guideline: Property Claims Handling Guidelines | 2. Water mitigation
hits.body:
2.1 On first contact for any water loss, confirm that the source has been stopped and tell the insured to begin drying out the home. Drying that starts within 48 hours prevents most mold.

hits.header: OPS-26-03 memo: Payments platform outage, May 11 to 22, 2026
hits.body:
To: All claims staff
From: Claims Operations
Date: June 8, 2026
Re: OPS-26-03, Payments platform outage, May 11 to 22, 2026

The payments platform failed to deliver claim payments issued from May 11 to 22, 2026. The 133 payments issued in that window, on 118 claims and totaling $953,540.43, were voided. Of these, 95 were indemnity payments and 38 were expense payments.

Each voided payment was reissued for the same amount to the same payee from May 26 to June 5, 2026. No claim was paid twice and none was paid less. Payees received their money two to three weeks late.

The voids and reissues distort paid-loss reports by payment date. A report that counts voided payments shows money in May that was never delivered, and one that ignores reissues misses it in late May and early June. Count reissued payments and exclude voided ones, which is how the reporting views are built.

If an insured or a vendor asks about a late payment from this period, confirm the reissue date on the claim and apologize for the delay. Section 6 of the claims handling guidelines covers how a voided payment is reissued.

hits.body:
To: Claims and underwriting staff, all regions
From: Personal Lines Underwriting
Date: November 15, 2024
Re: UW-25-01, HO-2025 edition: percentage wind and hail deductible

Form HO-2025 replaces HO-2023 for losses on or after January 1, 2025. The edition that applies is set by the date of loss, not the date the claim is reported, so a 2024 loss reported in 2025 is still handled under HO-2023.

In the West and South regions, the deductible for windstorm or hail becomes 2% of the Coverage A limit instead of a flat $1,000. On a home in Colorado at the state's median Coverage A of $414,000, the deductible for a wind or hail claim is now $8,280. On a home in Texas at the state's median Coverage A of $261,000, the deductible for a wind or hail claim is now $5,220. In the North and East regions, wind and hail keep the $1,000 deductible.

Two other terms change in every region. The fungi, mold and wet rot sublimit falls from $10,000 to $5,000, and a roof surface more than 15 years old on the date of loss is settled at actual cash value rather than replacement cost.

Expect fewer and larger wind and hail payments in the West and South regions from the spring of 2025, and more of those claims closed without payment because the damage falls below the deductible. Explain the deductible in dollars on first contact, so the insured is not surprised by the decision.

To: West region claims staff
From: Claims Cost Management
Date: October 15, 2025
Re: CL-25-14, Roofing labor and material costs, Denver metro, third quarter 2025

Roofing contractors in the Denver metro area raised their prices by about 22 percent for work billed from July 1 to September 30, 2025. The increase covers labor and materials alike. Crews are still committed to repairs from the April hail storm (CAT-25-07), and shingle and underlayment prices rose over the same months.

We reviewed the Colorado hail and wind claims closed in the quarter, 167 in all. Their repair costs run about 22 percent above what the same scope of work cost before July. The change is in the price of the work, not in the damage: the number of roofing squares and the items on the estimates are in line with earlier claims.

Do not question estimates that reflect the new prices. Reserve open Colorado roof claims at current prices, and use the price list dated July 1, 2025 in the estimating system. We will review again at the end of the fourth quarter.

To: West region claims staff
From: Claims Cost Management
Date: October 15, 2025
Re: CL-25-14, Roofing labor and material costs, Denver metro, third quarter 2025

Roofing contractors in the Denver metro area raised their prices by about 22 percent for work billed from July 1 to September 30, 2025. The increase covers labor and materials alike. Crews are still committed to repairs from the April hail storm (CAT-25-07), and shingle and underlayment prices rose over the same months.

We reviewed the Colorado hail and wind claims closed in the quarter, 167 in all. Their repair costs run about 22 percent above what the same scope of work cost before July. The change is in the price of the work, not in the damage: the number of roofing squares and the items on the estimates are in line with earlier claims.

Do not question estimates that reflect the new prices. Reserve open Colorado roof claims at current prices, and use the price list dated July 1, 2025 in the estimating system. We will review again at the end of the fourth quarter.

hits.body:
In case of a loss to covered property, we have no duty to provide coverage under this policy if the failure to comply with the following duties is prejudicial to us. You must see that the following are done:

hits.header: CG-2026 guideline: Property Claims Handling Guidelines | 3. Hail inspection procedure
hits.body:
3.1 Before the inspection, confirm from a hail verification report that hail fell at the property on the reported date of loss, and note the reported hail size.

hits.header: OPS-26-03 memo: Payments platform outage, May 11 to 22, 2026
hits.body:
To: All claims staff
From: Claims Operations
Date: June 8, 2026
Re: OPS-26-03, Payments platform outage, May 11 to 22, 2026

The payments platform failed to deliver claim payments issued from May 11 to 22, 2026. The 133 payments issued in that window, on 118 claims and totaling $953,540.43, were voided. Of these, 95 were indemnity payments and 38 were expense payments.

Each voided payment was reissued for the same amount to the same payee from May 26 to June 5, 2026. No claim was paid twice and none was paid less. Payees received their money two to three weeks late.

The voids and reissues distort paid-loss reports by payment date. A report that counts voided payments shows money in May that was never delivered, and one that ignores reissues misses it in late May and early June. Count reissued payments and exclude voided ones, which is how the reporting views are built.

If an insured or a vendor asks about a late payment from this period, confirm the reissue date on the claim and apologize for the delay. Section 6 of the claims handling guidelines covers how a voided payment is reissued.

hits.title: Payments platform outage, May 11 to 22, 2026
hits.header: OPS-26-03 memo: Payments platform outage, May 11 to 22, 2026
hits.body:
To: All claims staff
From: Claims Operations
Date: June 8, 2026
Re: OPS-26-03, Payments platform outage, May 11 to 22, 2026

The payments platform failed to deliver claim payments issued from May 11 to 22, 2026. The 133 payments issued in that window, on 118 claims and totaling $953,540.43, were voided. Of these, 95 were indemnity payments and 38 were expense payments.

Each voided payment was reissued for the same amount to the same payee from May 26 to June 5, 2026. No claim was paid twice and none was paid less. Payees received their money two to three weeks late.

The voids and reissues distort paid-loss reports by payment date. A report that counts voided payments shows money in May that was never delivered, and one that ignores reissues misses it in late May and early June. Count reissued payments and exclude voided ones, which is how the reporting views are built.

If an insured or a vendor asks about a late payment from this period, confirm the reissue date on the claim and apologize for the delay. Section 6 of the claims handling guidelines covers how a voided payment is reissued.

hits.title: Property Claims Handling Guidelines
hits.header: CG-2026 guideline: Property Claims Handling Guidelines | 6. Reissuing voided payments
hits.body:
6.1 A payment that was issued but never delivered is voided, and the same amount is reissued to the same payee. A reissue is not a new payment, and the reserve does not change because of it.

6.2 Record the void and the reissue on the claim, with the reference of the memo or incident that caused them.

6.3 Paid-loss figures count the reissued payment and exclude the voided one, so a void and its reissue together never change the amount paid on a claim.

6.4 Payments voided during the payments platform outage of May 2026 were reissued from May 26 to June 5, 2026, as set out in OPS-26-03.

hits.title: Property Claims Handling Guidelines
hits.header: CG-2026 guideline: Property Claims Handling Guidelines | 1. Reserving
hits.body:
1.1 Set the initial indemnity reserve within two business days of first contact, at your best estimate of what we will pay: the covered damage, less the deductible in force on the date of loss, capped by any sublimit.

1.2 Wind and hail losses in the West and South regions on or after January 1, 2025 carry the HO-2025 deductible of 2% of Coverage A. Net that amount from the reserve, not $1,000. On a dwelling insured for $400,000 the difference is $7,000.

1.3 A mold reserve never exceeds the sublimit of the edition in force: $10,000 under HO-2023 and $5,000 under HO-2025.

1.4 Review the reserve at every material change, such as a new estimate, a supplement or a coverage decision, and at least every 30 days while the claim is open. Record the reason for each change in a file note.

1.5 A reserve above your authority goes to your supervisor before it is posted. Adjuster authority is $25,000 per claim.

hits.body:
Escalate to your supervisor, and record the escalation in a file note, when any of the following applies.
